name: Finite Element Methods: Triqel
subtitle: Finite Element Methods Course
shortDescription: Adaptive finite element methods course: truss, bracket, fin, beam and quadrature in six 3D labs. Study aid only, not for real design.
longDescription:
Finite Element Methods: Triqel is an offline study app for a first university finite element methods course. Every topic starts from a real object: a footbridge, a steel bracket, a cooling fin, a diving board, a machine frame. It is for study only and is not for real design, safety or certification decisions.

### Six 3D Labs
- Convergence Bench: refine a rod mesh or raise the element degree and watch the error fall on a log-log chart.
- Footbridge Truss: tap a joint to move the load, tap a member to remove it, and see tension and compression in colour.
- Bracket Contours: stress contours painted per pixel on the GPU for an L-shaped bracket; compare element types and see locking and a sharp corner.
- Heat-Sink Fin: finite element temperature along a fin against the exact solution.
- Vibrating Beam: mode shapes and frequencies, animated, against the exact roots.
- Quadrature: a tapered four-node element with its integrand standing in 3D and Gauss points as weighted pillars.
Each lab opens its cited sources inside the app.

### Learn At Your Own Length And Level
- 14 topics from the weak form to isoparametric elements, locking and modelling practice.
- Quizzes, tests and a mock exam: choose 5, 10, 20, 40 or your own number of questions, and a level from beginner to research-level, adaptive or in course order.
- Numeric answers are checked against a second calculation engine; conceptual questions are marked practice-only.
- Worked explanations, A-/A+ text size, and it works offline.

### Free, With Optional Ad Removal
Free with ads at natural breaks, never in mock exams. An optional monthly subscription removes ads.
monetization: Free with ads, optional monthly ad-free
